title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: S is a base scheme and M is a rank-2 vector bundle on S. G = GL(M), SG = SL(M), PG = PGL(M), and P = P(M) is the associated P^1-bundle. In the 'équation des lacets' manuscript this setup serves the study of P^1-bundles with marked sections, the geometry behind the Teichmüller/Galois-action material.

The previous page sets up nilpotent sections N of End(M) with Tr N = 0 and det N = 0. Their homothety classes N' = aN, a ∈ Γ(O_S^*), are sections of the conic {det N = 0} in the projective plane bundle P(fM), where fM is the trace-zero part. Each N corresponds to e = 1+N, characterised by (3): det e = 1, Tr e = 2. By Cayley–Hamilton, (3) gives e^2 - 2e + 1 = 0, so N = e - 1 satisfies N^2 = 0.

This page:
- Sections of G (in fact of SG) satisfying (3) and nondegenerate fibrewise (e ≠ 1 at every point, i.e. N nowhere zero) are named, following Steinberg, 'regular unipotent' sections.
- Two such sections are declared equivalent (4) if e' = e^λ for a unit λ ∈ Γ(G_m). Here e^λ := 1 + λN, defined for any λ ∈ Γ(G_a) = Γ(O_S); it equals 1 + λ(e-1) = (1-λ) + λe. Since N^2 = 0, λ ↦ e^λ is a homomorphism G_a → SG, a one-parameter additive subgroup.
- Hence regular nilpotent sections of M (i.e. of End M) correspond bijectively to regular unipotent sections via N ↦ 1+N, and homothety of N corresponds to e ↦ e^λ.
- Equivalence classes correspond to Borel additive subgroups, i.e. unipotent radicals of Borel subgroups, of G, SG or PG (these are isomorphic via SG → PG).
- Taking normalisers, they correspond to Borel subgroups, i.e. to sections of P over S. Concretely, the line ker N = im N ⊂ M gives a point of P(M).
- Fix such a section x_∞ of P. Then E = P \ {x_∞} is an affine-line bundle (5), a torsor under a line bundle of translations. The next page identifies this with the subgroup L, L ≅ V(N), where N is the invertible sheaf spanned by the N's.

This is the standard dictionary: nilpotent element ↔ unipotent element ↔ unipotent radical ↔ Borel ↔ point of the flag variety, carried out relatively over S for rank 2. It prepares the description of P^1 minus a section as an affine line bundle on which the Borel acts by affine transformations.
errors: Globally the map {equivalence classes of regular unipotent sections} → {sections of P} is injective but not surjective. A section L ⊂ M lifts to a global N only if the invertible sheaf Hom(M/L, L) has a nowhere-vanishing section. So the correspondence holds locally on S or after sheafifying; the next page implicitly repairs this by passing to the line sheaf N and L ≅ V(N).
The transcribed condition '≡ 1 mod nilpotents' is redundant or garbled: (3) already forces e to be unipotent. What is needed for regularity is that e be nowhere equal to 1 (N fibrewise nonzero).

ideas.what: Regular unipotent elements and their correspondence (N ↔ 1+N) with regular nilpotents, under the condition det=1, Tr=2
ideas.modern_name: regular unipotent / nilpotent elements; Springer-type isomorphism for SL2
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 treats unipotent radicals and Borels over a base, but not this specific formulation

ideas.what: Classes of regular unipotent sections ↔ unipotent radicals of Borels ↔ Borels ↔ sections of the P^1-bundle
ideas.modern_name: Borel subgroups parametrised by the flag variety G/B; relative version over S
ideas.usually_credited_to: Borel, Chevalley; relative version in SGA 3 (Demazure–Grothendieck)
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 Exp. XXII–XXVI (scheme of Borel subgroups)

ideas.what: Complement of a section of a P^1-bundle is an affine-line bundle, a torsor under a line bundle

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but entirely standard relative Lie-theoretic dictionary for SL2/PGL2 over a base; serves as preparatory material.
transcription_corrections: The interlinear addition read as 'et qui sont ≡ 1 mod nilpotents' more plausibly reads something like 'et qui sont ≠ 1 en chaque point' (nowhere equal to 1), the regularity condition.
The marginal note is 'terminologie de Steinberg', attached to 'unipotentes régulières'.
'[-quotients-]' at the start is likely a struck-out word such as 'quelconques'; it does not change the meaning.
